messages.content: 約翰有5000美元想要投資。他正在考慮兩個選項。第一個選項是一個每年以4%的年利率按季度複利計算的儲蓄帳戶，為期5年。第二個選項是一個每年以3.5%的年利率提供單利的債券，為期5年。在5年後，約翰會有多少錢？

message.content:
**John’s two investment options**

| Option | Principal | Annual Rate | Compounding / Interest Type | Time |
|--------|-----------|-------------|----------------------------|------|
| **A – Savings account** | \$5 000 | 4 % p.a. | Quarterly compounding (`n = 4`) | 5 years |
| **B – Bond** | \$5 000 | 3.5 % p.a. | Simple interest | 5 years |

---

### 1️⃣ Future Value of the savings‑account (compound)

The compound‑interest formula is  

\[
FV_{\text{comp}} = P \left(1+\frac{r}{\,n}\right)^{n t}
\]

where  
\(P=\$5\,000,\; r=0.04,\; n=4,\; t=5.\)

\[
\begin{aligned}
FV_{\text{comp}}
&= 5\,000 \times \Bigl(1 + \tfrac{0.04}{4}\Bigr)^{4\times5}\\[4pt]
&= 5\,000 \times (1.01)^{20}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Using a precise calculator,

\[
(1.01)^{20} \approx 1.21899442 .
\]

Hence

\[
FV_{\text{comp}}\;\approx\;
5\,000 \times 1.21899442
\;\approx\;
\$6\,094.97 .
\]

> **After 5 years John will have roughly \$6 095 in the savings account.**

---

### 2️⃣ Future Value of the bond (simple interest)

Simple interest accumulates linearly:

\[
I = P \cdot r \cdot t ,
\qquad
FV_{\text{simp}} = P + I .
\]

With \(P=\$5\,000,\; r=0.035,\; t=5:\)

\[
\begin{aligned}
I &= 5\,000 \times 0.035 \times 5\\
  &= 5\,000 \times 0.175\\
  &= \$875 .
\end{aligned}
\]

Therefore

\[
FV_{\text{simp}} = 5\,000 + 875 = \$5\,875 .
\]

> **After 5 years John will have \$5 875 on the bond.**

---

## 📊 Comparison & Recommendation

| Option | Final Amount |
|--------|--------------|
| Savings account (quarterly comp.) | **~\$6 095** |
| Bond (simple interest) | **\$5 875** |

Because the savings account compounds each quarter, it grows faster—by about **\$220** more than the bond does over the five‑year horizon.

If your goal is simply maximizing the dollar amount you’ll receive after five years, the **savings account** is the superior choice under the given terms.

---

Would you like help exploring other scenarios (different rates, longer periods, tax considerations, etc.), or perhaps setting up a spreadsheet template to track this yourself? Let me know!
